svg.aria-label: Collagen triple helix: three protein chains, drawn in red, blue and green, wind around each other into a rope-like right-handed triple helix. A box explains the repeating unit Gly-X-Y, where X is often proline and Y is often hydroxyproline; every third residue is glycine, small enough to fit in the crowded center. Hydrogen bonds between chains hold the helix together, and making hydroxyproline requires vitamin C.

g.title: Collagen triple helix: three protein chains, drawn in red, blue and green, wind around each other into a rope-like right-handed triple helix. A box explains the repeating unit Gly-X-Y, where X is often proline and Y is often hydroxyproline; every third residue is glycine, small enough to fit in the crowded center. Hydrogen bonds between chains hold the helix together, and making hydroxyproline requires vitamin C.
g.text: Collagen: a triple helix of three protein chains
Three left-handed chains wind around each other into a right-handed "rope."
Repeating unit
Gly – X – Y
X is often proline (Pro)
Y is often hydroxyproline (Hyp)
Every third residue is glycine, the
smallest amino acid, so it fits in
the crowded center of the helix.
Hydrogen bonds between the chains hold the triple helix together. Making hydroxyproline needs vitamin C;
without it, collagen is weak (scurvy).
